## Where we are

The model hands us a **probability distribution** over the next token.

How we draw from it is *our* decision — made per API call, with three knobs:

- `temperature` — reshape the distribution
- `top_p` — cut off its tail
- `max_tokens` — cap the output

::::

## Step 1 — A model we're allowed to experiment on

Reasoning-first models (the `gpt-5` family) fix their sampling internally and
ignore these knobs, so we switch to a standard chat model:

```{.python code-line-numbers="3"}
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model

sampler = init_chat_model(model="gpt-4.1-mini")
```

## Step 2 — A helper that repeats the same prompt

Sampling is random — a single call proves nothing. We always look at several draws:

```{.python code-line-numbers="1-4|6"}
def sample_n(prompt, n=4, **model_kwargs):
    """Call the model n times with the same settings."""
    m = init_chat_model(model="gpt-4.1-mini", **model_kwargs)
    return [m.invoke(prompt).content.strip() for _ in range(n)]

prompt = "Invent a name for a coffee shop run by robots. Reply with the name only."
```

:::: {.content-visible when-format="revealjs"}
::: {.notes}
Walk the highlight: signature → constructor with kwargs → the n draws → the call.
Ask the class to predict outputs before advancing.
:::
::::

## Step 3 — Cold vs. hot

Before running: **write down what you expect** at `0.0` versus `1.4`.

```{.python}
for out in sample_n(prompt, temperature=0.0):   # <1>
    print("  •", out)

for out in sample_n(prompt, temperature=1.4):   # <2>
    print("  •", out)
```
1. Near-greedy: sharpened distribution — expect (almost) identical names.
2. Flattened distribution: tail tokens get a vote — variety, occasionally nonsense.

## Step 3 — What you should see

Your output won't match your neighbor's exactly (that's the lesson), but the
shape should look like this:

```text
temperature = 0.0          temperature = 1.4
  • Brew Bots                • Circuit & Crema
  • Brew Bots                • The Rusty Filament
  • Brew Bots                • Steamwork Sips
  • Brew Bots                • Perky Processor
```

## Step 4 — What to remember {.smaller}

| Setting | Use when | Avoid when |
|---|---|---|
| `temperature` 0–0.3 | tool calls, extraction, agents | brainstorming |
| `temperature` 0.8–1.2 | idea generation, drafts | anything schema-bound |
| `top_p` < 1 | trimming the weird tail | tuning together with high temperature |

::: {.callout-important title="The rule I'll keep repeating"}
Agents loop. A 2% weirdness rate per step compounds across 20 steps into roughly
a one-in-three chance of a derailed trajectory. Keep agent temperature low; save
the high settings for steps that are supposed to diverge.
:::
